notes: NCBI Bookshelf Glucagonoma was verified at its May 3, 2025 update for alpha-cell origin, glucagon excess, cAMP-mediated hepatic glycogenolysis/gluconeogenesis, hyperglycemia, weight loss, and necrolytic migratory erythema.
NCBI Bookshelf Necrolytic Migratory Erythema was verified for the characteristic glucagonoma association and lesion distribution/presentation.
NCBI Bookshelf physiology pages for insulin, VIP, gastrin, and somatostatin were verified claim-by-claim for all four distractors.

The official USMLE Content Outline (2026) was verified at Endocrine System — diabetes mellitus and other disorders of the endocrine pancreas — hyperglycemia secondary to glucagonoma / pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
official_outline_path: Diabetes mellitus and other disorders of the endocrine pancreas

claim_audit.diagnostic_pattern: Hyperglycemia, progressive weight loss, necrolytic migratory erythema, and a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor support glucagonoma syndrome.
claim_audit.key_mechanism: Glucagon activates hepatic Gs/adenylyl cyclase/cAMP signaling and increases glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
claim_audit.insulin_distractor: Insulin receptor tyrosine kinase signaling promotes GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake and opposes hepatic glucose production; it is not the hyperglucagonemic mechanism.
claim_audit.vip_distractor: VIP activates VPAC-cAMP signaling in the intestine and causes secretory water/electrolyte loss, producing the VIPoma phenotype rather than NME.
claim_audit.gastrin_distractor: Gastrin activates CCK-B signaling on parietal/ECL cells and increases gastric acid secretion, producing acid-peptic disease rather than glucagonoma syndrome.
claim_audit.somatostatin_distractor: Somatostatin excess suppresses insulin and CCK/gallbladder emptying and can produce diabetes, steatorrhea, and cholelithiasis, but NME is not the defining syndrome.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Without using the staged key, the constellation of a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, catabolic weight loss, new hyperglycemia, and a migratory erythematous scaly eruption in characteristic frictional/periorificial regions identifies glucagon excess. The physiologic consequence most directly linked to glucagon is hepatic cAMP-driven glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
adversarial_second_pass.somatostatin_challenge: Somatostatinoma can cause diabetes and weight loss, but the vignette lacks steatorrhea/cholelithiasis and instead contains the highly discriminating necrolytic migratory erythema pattern. Its mechanism therefore is not a defensible second answer.
adversarial_second_pass.vip_challenge: VIP can raise cAMP but primarily in intestinal secretory pathways and should produce profuse watery diarrhea with electrolyte loss; the vignette does not support that syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.gastrin_challenge: Gastrinoma would require acid hypersecretion/ulcer disease rather than the rash-hyperglycemia pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.insulin_challenge: Insulin excess produces hypoglycemia, directly opposing the vignette's hyperglycemia.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All alternatives are physiologic hormone effects at comparable mechanistic specificity. The correct choice is not uniquely longer, grammatically linked, or echoed verbatim by the stem.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No glucagon concentration, glucose cutoff, tumor-size threshold, rash prevalence, metastatic rate, or treatment rule is required. The age is contextual only.
